Description:
As an employee, I want to clock in when I start my workday and clock out when I finish, so that my working hours are recorded accurately without manual timesheets.

Business value: Removes manual/paper attendance tracking and gives HR a reliable, real-time record of who is working and when.
Acceptance Criteria:
- I can clock in once per day and see a confirmation with the timestamp
- I can clock out any time after clocking in
- If I forget to clock out, the system flags it as an incomplete entry for follow-up
- I can see my own attendance history for the current month

As a manager, I want to see who on my team is present, absent, or late today, so that I can plan work and staffing without chasing people for updates.

Business value: Gives managers a single view of team availability instead of relying on Slack/email check-ins.
Acceptance Criteria:
- A team attendance view shows each direct report's status for the current day (present, absent, late, on leave)
- The view updates as employees clock in/out
- Only a manager's own direct/indirect reports are visible to them

As an employee, I want to request time off and have my manager approve or reject it, so that my absence is planned and reflected in attendance records.

Business value: Replaces ad-hoc leave requests over email/chat with a trackable, auditable approval process.
Acceptance Criteria:
- An employee can submit a leave request with dates and a reason
- The employee's manager receives the request and can approve or reject it with a comment
- Approved leave automatically marks the employee as 'On Leave' for those dates in attendance records
- The employee is notified of the decision

As an employee, I want to request a correction when I forget to clock in or out, so that my attendance record reflects the day accurately instead of showing an absence.

Business value: Reduces disputes and manual HR intervention caused by forgotten punches.
Acceptance Criteria:
- An employee can submit a regularization request for a specific date with a reason and the correct times
- The request routes to their manager for approval
- Approved regularizations update the attendance record and are marked as 'Regularized' (distinct from a normal punch) for audit purposes

As an HR administrator, I want to define a company-wide holiday calendar, so that employees are automatically marked as not working on holidays without needing to request leave.

Business value: Avoids employees being incorrectly flagged as absent on holidays and reduces unnecessary leave requests.
Acceptance Criteria:
- HR can add/edit/remove holidays with a date and name
- Attendance for any employee on a holiday date is automatically marked 'Holiday', not 'Absent'
- Holidays are visible to all employees in a shared calendar view

As an HR administrator, I want to define work shifts and assign employees to them, so that attendance is evaluated against each employee's expected working hours rather than a single fixed schedule.

Business value: Supports teams with different working hours (e.g. day shift, night shift) instead of assuming one schedule for everyone.
Acceptance Criteria:
- HR can create shifts with a start time, end time, and name
- Each employee can be assigned to a shift
- 'Late' and 'early departure' flags are calculated relative to the employee's assigned shift, not a global default

As an HR administrator, I want a monthly attendance summary per employee (days present, absent, on leave, late), so that I can use it for payroll processing and compliance reporting without manually compiling data.

Business value: Removes manual spreadsheet work HR currently does each pay cycle and reduces payroll errors from missed attendance data.
Acceptance Criteria:
- A report can be generated for a selected month, for one employee or the whole company
- The report breaks down days present, absent, on leave, holiday, and late arrivals
- The report can be exported (e.g. CSV) for use in payroll

Summary: Sync employee roster from Employee Management System
Description:
As an HR administrator, I want new hires and role/department changes from the Employee Management System to automatically reflect in the attendance service, so that attendance records always match the current employee roster without duplicate data entry.

Business value: Prevents attendance gaps or mismatches caused by keeping employee data in two systems manually.
Acceptance Criteria:
- When an employee is added, updated, or marked terminated in the Employee Management System, the attendance service reflects that change
- A terminated employee can no longer clock in
- Department/manager changes are reflected in the manager's team attendance view

Summary: Record employee attendance for the first time
Description:
As an employee, I want to clock in and clock out so that my working hours are actually recorded, not just planned as a feature.

Business value: This is the very first working capability of the Attendance Service — every other attendance feature (leave, approvals, reports) depends on attendance actually being recorded somewhere first. This story should be delivered before any other attendance story.
Acceptance Criteria:
- I can clock in once per day and see a confirmation
- I can clock out after clocking in
- My clock-in and clock-out are saved and still there if I check back later
- I can see my own attendance for the current month
